$comment: Coordinator operations of the sessions domain; the rules are in ops.schema.json $comment and contracts/README.md.

session_view.description: One conversation screen (sessionId): the head, the composer target, open questions, triggers, the context panel, the last message and the newest executions as summaries (page older ones with executionsBefore). No stored snapshots, dispatch or tool output: open a tool call with tool_output, an execution with execution_get.

tool_output.description: The input and output of one tool call (callId from a thread_entries tool block), loaded when the call is opened.

approval_ask.description: Before a radical action (LIVE deploy, deleting or banning accounts, messages to real users, keys, money, dropping data) ask for approval and wait: Fleet rates the action by the project's risk rules (settings.risks, settings.approvals); a radical one becomes an approval card (a question with Approve / Not now, shown in its Telegram room and in Needs you) naming exactly what, where, version and rollback. Call again with the same requestId after the reply arrives to read the state; a changed scope withdraws the old card and asks again. Free and reversible actions answer not-needed: do them and report (reversible: say how to undo). Never take keys or secrets from chat: point to System > Access.

ask.description: For a persistent CI or delivery access or diagnostic blocker use publishing_report_blocker. Otherwise ask a fresh question with question + requestId and taskId for an existing-task blocker (without attaching the PM session), or read its answer with resume=<questionId> alone; never combine these modes or put continuation prose in resume

changes_since.description: No cursor: the head, with no changes. limit is clamped to 1..1000 (default 500).

direct_search.description: Run a direct search using an enabled method from catalogue for the selected project. Omit methodId to use the project recommendation. Idempotent by requestId.

message_send.description: Send a message to a session. For a host agent, allowed targets are its current session and sessions created by that session. Fleet bots may also target their own bot conversations and sessions linked to tasks they created or manage. Omit sessionId to target the host agent's current session. Omit delivery for an ordinary message, which starts a turn when the session is ready and queues for a later turn when it is busy. Set delivery to steer to steer an eligible running turn. Where the input schema includes attachments, pass artifact IDs from the target session's project (artifact_save output or an operator upload). The receiving agent gets those files under FLEET_INPUT_DIR/attachments and sees them listed in its turn. Messages with attachments use ordinary delivery.

recommendation_set.description: Set the recommended method of a project's capability (projectId, methodId)

reply.description: Answer a question; delivered to the asker as its next message

session_archive.description: Archive a session (sessionId): it leaves the lists and its worktree is torn down

session_context.description: What a session (sessionId) plans and keeps running, for the context panel: plan (steps with done marks, owner and task from its work_plan, else its task's), swarm members (the plan's and board's other sessions with their state) and tasks (its own task, the plan's tasks, the tasks it spawned and its bot's tasks; a task's own change does not reread it). Each part is empty when the session has none. Its timers and its bot's automations are triggers: trigger_list {sessionId} and {botId}

session_fork.description: Fork a session (native fork when the host supports it, else context transfer); the original stays unchanged, also for sessions stuck in unknown

session_get.description: A session (sessionId) with its executions and state

session_handoffs.description: Context handoffs of a session with delivery state

session_presets.description: Presets for starting a session in a project (projectId; a person may omit it for outside projects, an agent reads its own project): id, name, what it does, the role or profile it resolves to (a system profile when the project does not map the role; an agent starts only profiles its project maps), access read|write, branch, starter instruction; unavailable says why one cannot start. Start with session_start preset=<id>

session_profile.description: Change a session's profile (sessionId, profileId, optional account and workingDirectory)

session_rename.description: Name a conversation (sessionId, default your own; title up to 200 characters, no UUID). An explicit title is kept: the generated title never replaces it

session_update.description: Change a conversation (sessionId, default your own): projectIds, its project set (project ids in your grants; with one project it is the default projectId of task_create and session_start, as focus_set). The same set focus_set writes; the conversation's checkout project (projectId) stays

session_resume.description: Native resume/fork argv and captured native sessions for a session

session_start.description: Start a new session in a project: projectId, requestId, preset (an id from session_presets: its role or profile, access, branch and starter) or role (project roles map) or profileId, optional access read|write and branch true|false (override the preset; default write with a branch), account/hostId, taskId (the session works for that task of the project), subject (what the conversation is about: task:<id>, question:<id>, pr:<repo>#<n>, host:<id>, delivery:<id> or trigger:<id>; it titles the conversation, and one profile and role keep one open conversation per subject: 409 names it), projects (the project set, as session_update), text, attachments (artifact ids, as message_send), setup run|skip. The creator is woken when it finishes

session_task_attach.description: Attach a taskless non-bot conversation to a task (sessionId, taskId). Earlier turns join the task thread without copying. All bot conversations are ineligible, including problem conversations. Use the bot's managed task links or problem_update to link work on a problem.

session_transition.description: Select this session’s granted project checkout with projectId, or switch profileId/account (profileId defaults to current). A changed project selection during an active execution returns queued: end this turn; Fleet applies it and automatically starts the next execution to continue the request with frozen context. Focus is separate (focus_set). Other transitions return reuse|switch_model_in_session|restart_and_resume|create_with_handoff

session_unarchive.description: Owner or full-access person. Returns an archived session to the lists; a setting-change row records the reason. A worktree already torn down is not restored; the next start prepares a new one.

sessions_list.description: after: the nextAfter of the previous page.

thread_blocks.description: rows: changed records; the reply has their current blocks.

thread_composer.description: Resolve the current message and Stop target from the open conversation, independent of the transcript page.

thread_entries.description: Entries of a thread (key), paged with before, after or around and limit

thread_export.description: A thread (key) as text, optionally between from and to in timezone tz

thread_search.description: Find text in a thread (key, q), paged with before and limit

session_command.description: Run a composer command for a session (sessionId): text such as `/trigger conversation-check every 10m if changed: <message>` (also pause, resume, run, delete, and `/trigger new <preset> [as <name>] ...`), through trigger_save, trigger_delete or trigger_run. With baseRevision (the preview's) and triggerId, answers 409 when that trigger changed since. A trigger is named by its name in the session (lower case, spaces as '-'), else by its id; a name two triggers share asks for the id. session_command_preview shows what it will do first.

session_command_preview.description: What session_command would do with text, nothing saved: the trigger it names as it is now (with its revision) and the changes, field by field. With format (a trigger id) instead of text: the command that sets that trigger to what it is now, for Edit.

trigger_delete.description: Delete a trigger (id) at its current revision (baseRevision).

trigger_list.description: The triggers of a session (sessionId) or a bot (botId): what each sends, when (every, daily, manual), its change condition (ifChanged), state (next time, fires, quiet checks since the last fire, last error), whether you may manage them, and the presets (config/triggers).

trigger_run.description: Fire a trigger (id) now, whatever its time and change condition say.

trigger_save.description: Create (baseRevision 0, a new UUID id, sessionId or botId) or change a trigger. settings fields left out come from the preset (presetId) on create, else stay. A trigger puts its text into the session, or wakes the bot, at its time (when: every everyMs, daily dailyTime dailyZone, manual); with ifChanged (task, question, execution, host, limits) it fires only when something in its focus changed since it last fired and otherwise only counts a quiet check. Pause: enabled false.

worker_done.description: Report the current execution done (checked against the current execution; captures native session)

tools.$comment: The profile's tool allowlist; empty: the harness tools.

SessionAgent.$comment: The session's agent profile as the composer chips show it; the stored configuration stays on the server.

ToolKind.$comment: What a tool call works on, for its chip and fold; the server classifies with the rules of packages/ui/src/controls/tool-fold.ts toolKind().

reason.$comment: Why no message can be sent now; null when one can.

agent.$comment: The target session's agent; absent without a target.

SessionComposer.$comment: The session that receives the next message and the run Stop stops (thread_composer's answer).

executionsBefore.$comment: Page: executions with seq below this.

questions.$comment: Open questions of this session and of the composer target.

lastMessage.$comment: For Retry; absent before the first message.

botTriggers.$comment: trigger_list {botId} for a bot's Home: its automations; absent otherwise.

title.$comment: The set or generated title, else the first message's start, else New conversation.

state.$comment: State of the latest visible agent run, or idle; follows the live run through the change stream.

error.$comment: The latest run's error, one line.

subject.$comment: What it is about: task:<id>, question:<id>, pr:<repo>#<n>, host:<id>, delivery:<id>, trigger:<id>.

source.$comment: What started the turn: person, trigger, wake, needs_you, watch.

ExecutionSummary.$comment: One turn as a row: no snapshots, dispatch or configuration; execution_get has the whole record and its spend.

ApprovalAction.$comment: Action classes of approval_ask; settings.risks of a project may rate any of them free, reversible or radical.

requestId.$comment: One id per action; the same id reads the card's state.

what.$comment: Exactly what will change, as the asker understood it (ban 114 accounts of the Nov 23-24 campaign).

version.$comment: The exact commit, release or data set.

taskId.$comment: Fresh ask about this granted task; does not attach the PM session. Omit for a session-only question or bound-worker inference.

question.$comment: Fresh ask text. Requires requestId; do not combine with resume.

resume.$comment: Existing question ID to read, never continuation prose. Do not combine with question or requestId.

Block.$comment: One thread entry (docs/designs/fleet-conversations.md), told apart by kind. key is its position seq:part. Fleet's own projection: closed.

waitReason.$comment: a run not started or waiting: its wait kind (dispatch.go waitReasons)

waitDetail.$comment: a run not started or waiting: why, naming the constraint (docs/designs/fleet-people-access.md#6-dispatch, Blocked reason is visible)

BoundaryBlock.$comment: Start of an execution in the thread.

touches.$comment: The operations whose reply this change can alter: each operation whose contract changes names this kind (and id prefix). The app rereads a mounted read when its operation is touched and the change names no other entity of its request.

settingTarget.$comment: For setting-change only: exact audit target captured with the change, e.g. person:<email>, independently of actor. Missing/null legacy metadata requires conservative preference reread. Definition IDs retain kind/id scope; unknown legacy IDs remain conservative.

Change.$comment: One committed change (the change table), as GET /api/stream and changes_since deliver it.

ChangesSinceReply.$comment: resync: the cursor fell out of retention, reload everything. held: a writer still holds older changes; read again.

ChangesSinceRequest.$comment: No cursor: the head, with no changes. limit is clamped to 1..1000 (default 500).

DirectSearchReply.$comment: A pipeline run with its steps, state and results (pipelineRun).

DirectSearchRequest.$comment: Runs the project's method for a capability (pipeline_run) or a direct search; idempotent by requestId.

MessageSendReply.$comment: The execution the message started, or the queued message with queued: true and its position.

attachments.$comment: Artifact ids (artifact_upload_begin, artifact_save) of the session project; the executor stages them under FLEET_INPUT_DIR/attachments and lists them in the turn.

sentBy.$comment: Accepted and ignored: the sender is the caller (or Fleet for its own timer, change and wake inputs), never an argument.

source.$comment: Accepted and ignored from a caller: Fleet sets it for its own inputs.

QuestionBlock.$comment: options: the stored options as they are (a list of labels for agent questions).

ReplyReply.$comment: The answered agent question record with its delivery.

previewId.$comment: The stored preview (a thumbnail, else a video poster) the thread shows inline; absent when there is none.

ResultBlock.$comment: The stored artifacts and observed publishing stage of an ended execution.

SessionArchiveReply.$comment: {sessionId, archivedAt, teardown: null} when no execution is left to tear down, else the teardown command it queued (id, executionId, hostId, kind teardown, payload, status).

SessionCreateReply.$comment: The new session row, plus sessionId.

SessionCreateRequest.$comment: No fields: the session's director, access and linkage come from the caller.

reason.$comment: Why Fleet selected the fork strategy; absent in legacy records.

state.$comment: State of the latest visible agent run, or idle.

title.$comment: Set by session_rename or generated after the first reply (docs/designs/fleet-conversations.md, Titles); absent until then.

titleBy.$comment: auto for a generated title, else the person or agent that set it.

titleCall.$comment: The tool_run id of the model call that generated the current title (its tokens and cost); absent for a title a person or agent set.

access.$comment: read or write; null: started before presets (write).

branch.$comment: false: no session branch; null: started before presets (a branch).

starter.$comment: The preset instruction added to every turn.

SessionGetReply.$comment: The session view: the session row with its executions, questions, focus, handoffs, cost and scoped resources.

SessionExecution.$comment: An execution record of the session as stored (agent.go sessionExecutions); lastSeenAt is ms or RFC 3339 by age.

waitDetail.$comment: why it has not started: the skip reason of dispatch

SessionQuestion.$comment: A question record of the session as stored.

SessionMessage.$comment: A message record of the session as stored.

SessionProfileReply.$comment: transition, handoffId and nativeSessionId only when the session has a native session to move.

titleBy.$comment: The person or agent that set it.

sessionId.$comment: Required from people; a host agent's call defaults to its own session.

title.$comment: 1 to 200 characters after whitespace is collapsed; no UUID (OR-38).

SessionRenameRequest.$comment: The explicit title of a conversation; a person renames one they direct (403 otherwise; the owner any). A generated title (titleBy auto) never replaces it and is never written over it.

sessionId.$comment: Required from people; a host agent's call defaults to its own session.

projectIds.$comment: The new project set (session.payload focus.projectIds); empty: the checkout project alone (the focus is dropped).

SessionUpdateRequest.$comment: A person changes a conversation they direct (403 otherwise; the owner any), like session_rename. A call without a field to change is a 400.

projectIds.$comment: The project set after the call: focus.projectIds, else the checkout project.

SessionResumeReply.$comment: How the session continues: its harness, account and native session ids.

SessionStartReply.$comment: existing: the requestId already started this session.

siteTargetId.$comment: Explicit production site target eligible for this project role and run scope.

attachments.$comment: Artifact ids (artifact_upload_begin, artifact_save) of the session project; the executor stages them under FLEET_INPUT_DIR/attachments and lists them in the turn.

branch.$comment: false: no session branch (a detached worktree); default true, or the preset's.

preset.$comment: A preset id of session_presets for this project: its role or profile, access, branch and starter apply; explicit role, profileId, access and branch override it.

projectId.$comment: Absent (people only): a conversation outside projects, with the system presets.

subject.$comment: task:<id>, question:<id>, pr:<repo>#<n>, host:<id>, delivery:<id> or trigger:<id>; titles the conversation. 409 while the same profile and role keep an open conversation about it.

projects.$comment: The project set (session_update projectIds); absent: the checkout project alone.

SessionAccess.$comment: read: the agent may read and run read-only tools but not change files (StartPayload.readOnly); write: the profile's own grant.

role.$comment: The project role the preset resolved to; null when it fell back to a system profile.

starter.$comment: Instruction added to every turn of the session, after the profile's.

unavailable.$comment: Why the preset cannot start here (no such profile); null when it can.

SessionPresetSource.$comment: project: settings.presets of the project; system: the defaults Fleet ships.

projectId.$comment: Absent: the system presets for a conversation outside projects.

branchPrefix.$comment: The project's session branch prefix (worktree.branchPrefix); null outside projects.

base.$comment: What a new worktree starts from: worktree.baseRef, origin/<defaultBranch> or HEAD; the executor falls back to HEAD when the fetch fails. null outside projects.

SessionPresetsReply.$comment: The project's presets (settings.presets) or the system defaults, each resolved to a profile: its role when the project maps it, else the preset's system profile.

SessionUnarchiveReply.$comment: teardownsWithdrawn: pending teardown commands of the session that were stopped before a host ran them.

SessionUnarchiveRequest.$comment: Owner or full-access person. Returns an archived session to the lists; a setting-change row records the reason. A worktree already torn down is not restored; the next start prepares a new one.

origins.$comment: First page only: the conversations of this filter by origin, the origin filter left out (the Started by chips).

hiddenCount.$comment: First page only: the hidden conversations (pipeline and Lab agent steps) of this filter, the origin and listed filters left out (the Steps toggle).

SessionsListReply.$comment: nextAfter: null on the last page, else the sort key to pass as after. Row sortKey: [group key, sort key, id]; rows carry activityAt (last change of the session, its messages and events, or the start or end of its executions) and executions (their count). groups: key, label and count of each group of the filtered list (none for group none).

group.$comment: project, state, agent, room or none; agent groups by the conversation model: the bot, else the Telegram room, else the PM of the project, else none (keys b:, r:, p:, ~); room by the Telegram room; default project, with the waiting sessions first as one group (key empty, label waiting); state groups in attention order (waiting, failed, running, preparing, idle, succeeded, cancelled)

sort.$comment: order inside a group: last activity or creation, - before it is descending; default -activity (latest activity first)

SessionsListRequest.$comment: after: the nextAfter of the previous page.

TextBlock.$comment: role agent or operator; by: the sender of an operator message; attachments: the files an operator message carried; stream open or cut-off while a delta is the newest text; harness, model and effort mark agent text.

ThreadBlocksReply.$comment: removed: block keys that no longer exist.

full.$comment: As thread_entries full: default true; false keeps tool blocks to their summary.

ThreadBlocksRequest.$comment: rows: changed records; the reply has their current blocks.

ThreadComposerSelection.$comment: The open conversation and displayed target execution (null for Message). A new write fails if the composer target changed. A retained requestId reconciles against the original destination.

ThreadEntriesReply.$comment: total: only with around. feedCursor: the change cursor of this read, to catch up from.

full.$comment: Default true: tool blocks carry their input and output. false: summaries only (callId, toolKind, target, errorLine); tool_output loads one call when it is opened.

ThreadKey.$comment: Exactly one of task or session.

target.$comment: A short readable target: a code or name instead of a UUID, a path relative to the workspace.

errorLine.$comment: The first error line, only when the call failed.

ToolBlock.$comment: input and output are the harness's own values, absent when thread_entries asks full: false (tool_output loads them for one call). callId, toolKind, target and errorLine are always set. Times in ms.

botId.$comment: the bot whose home session this is: its automations are trigger_list {botId}

SessionContextReply.$comment: session_context (session_context.go). plan absent: no work plan on the session or its task.

SessionPlan.$comment: The work_plan's tasks in thread order, one step each.

owner.$comment: the roster member the step is assigned to

SessionTask.$comment: A task related to the session, as its entity card names it.

ifChanged.$comment: change kinds: task, question, execution, host, limits; empty: fire on time

TriggerSettingsInput.$comment: A field left out comes from the preset on create, else keeps its value.

nextAt.$comment: RFC 3339; absent: paused, manual, or not computable

quietChecks.$comment: checks without a change since the last fire

lastRun.$comment: bot targets: the last bot run this trigger caused

TriggerPreset.$comment: config/triggers/<id>.json: the values trigger_save copies into a new trigger.

passMs.$comment: the pass interval (FLEET_TRIGGER_TICK_MS): a trigger every this often or less checks each pass, so it follows changes rather than a clock

triggerId.$comment: the trigger baseRevision is of; another trigger named by text is not checked

format.$comment: a trigger id: answer its command in text instead of reading one

text.$comment: the command; for format, the trigger's own

action.$comment: edit, pause, resume, run, delete, new, format

title.$comment: what the command does, such as Change trigger conversation-check

trigger.$comment: preview: the trigger as it is; run: as saved. Absent for new before it runs and after delete

sent.$comment: run: whether the trigger put its text into the session
false: the target is busy or the bot skipped the wake (paused, active run); see bot_runs

WorkerDoneReply.$comment: action accepted (with the report) or rejected (with code: invalid_outcome, stale_dispatch, already_reported, native_identity_conflict, and reason).

liveCheck.$comment: Exact delivery verification key from Fleet; include affirmative check evidence in summary.

WorkerDoneRequest.$comment: outcome succeeded or failed; anything else is recorded as rejected (invalid_outcome). summary: a string; any other value is stored as null.
